mainEntity.name: Do porcelain veneers change colour as I get older?

acceptedAnswer.text: Porcelain veneers themselves are highly resistant to staining and do not change colour in the same way natural teeth do. However, the bonding resin at the margins can yellow slightly over time, and surrounding natural teeth may darken, creating a contrast that was not there originally. This is one of the most common cosmetic concerns patients raise in mid-to-late life about existing veneers. A dental professional can assess whether the veneer shade still harmonises with the rest of your smile and advise on appropriate options.

mainEntity.name: How long do dental veneers typically last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of dental veneers varies depending on the material and individual factors. Porcelain veneers, when well cared for, may last between ten and twenty years in many cases, though longevity varies depending on individual clinical and lifestyle factors. Composite veneers typically have a shorter lifespan and may require replacement or repair sooner. Oral hygiene habits, dietary choices, any grinding habits, and the quality of the original bonding all influence longevity. Your dentist can give you a more personalised estimate based on the current condition of your veneers during a clinical review.

mainEntity.name: Can receding gums make veneers look worse?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, gum recession can affect the appearance of veneers noticeably. As the gumline retreats, the margin between the veneer and the natural tooth surface may become more visible, creating a line or shadow that was not apparent when the veneers were first placed. In some cases, the root surface of the tooth — which is a different shade to enamel — may also become partially exposed. Addressing gum health is therefore an important part of maintaining a consistent smile appearance over time. A general dental check-up can assess the health of your gums alongside your veneers.

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to replace or update ageing veneers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, veneers can be replaced when they reach the end of their lifespan or when the aesthetic result is no longer satisfactory. The process involves removing the existing veneer and placing a new one, with the new shade matched carefully to your current teeth or updated according to your preferences. Whether replacement is appropriate and what it involves depends on the condition of the underlying tooth and the surrounding dental structures. This would always be assessed during a clinical examination before any treatment is planned.

mainEntity.name: Will teeth whitening help if my veneers look different from my natural teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Teeth whitening can brighten natural teeth, but it does not change the shade of porcelain or composite veneers. If your natural teeth have darkened and now appear noticeably different from your veneers, whitening surrounding teeth could potentially improve the overall harmony — but this needs to be managed carefully to avoid overcorrecting and creating a reverse mismatch. It is essential to discuss any whitening plans with your dentist before proceeding, especially when existing veneers are present, so that a coordinated approach can be taken.

mainEntity.name: At what age do veneers typically start looking more noticeable?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed age at which veneers begin to stand out. It depends on factors such as the age at which the veneers were placed, the rate of natural tooth ageing, oral hygiene practices, diet, and lifestyle habits. Some patients notice subtle changes in their late thirties or forties; for others, it is not until later decades. Each person's experience is individual. Regular dental reviews are the most effective way to monitor changes over time and address them at an early stage.
